question:
Which of the following is equal to the product

\[ \begin{aligned} &\dfrac{8}{4} \cdot \dfrac{12}{8} \cdot \dfrac{16}{12} \cdots \dfrac{4n+4}{4n} \\ &\quad \cdots \dfrac{2008}{2004}? \end{aligned} \]
solution:
Each numerator except the last is the denominator of the next fraction. Thus every number from \(8\) through \(2004\) appearing in the product cancels once above and once below. All these numbers are positive, so the cancellations are valid. Only the first denominator, \(4\), and the last numerator, \(2008\), remain:
\[
\frac84\cdot\frac{12}{8}\cdot\frac{16}{12}\cdots\frac{2008}{2004}
=\frac{2008}{4}=502.
\]
The answer is \(502\), choice \(B\).

edges.reason: The assertion that the fraction's value stays unchanged requires interpreting the fraction's represented quantity.

The integer-multiplier case supplies a useful stepping stone and repeated-addition interpretation. The product-of-numerators/product-of-denominators rule follows directly from a part-of-a-part area model without executing the earlier decimal-free integer-multiplier procedure; Gemini confuses this customary progression with necessity.
Rational arithmetic helps evaluate surviving endpoint terms in fraction examples. The cancellation idea is structural and applies to symbolic, radical or other terms.
